title: Generic direct image has invertible counit
statement: Let $D$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with function field $K$ and generic inclusion $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to D$ [def-sc-function-field]. For any abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the counit $\eta^{-1}\eta_*F\to F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For a geometric point of Spec k(D), identify its image with the generic point of D. The local ring there is the function field, and its strict henselization is a separable closure. The generic inclusion is qcqs (it is affine: its restriction over an affine open is either the empty scheme or the spectrum of the fraction field). Its base change to this strict henselization is the identity. The degree-zero strict-henselization stalk comparison thus identifies the geometric stalk of eta_*F with that of F.

Inverse image preserves geometric stalks, so the source of the counit at that point is the stalk of eta_*F at its image. The germ restriction formula for the counit identifies its stalk map with the comparison just computed, hence this map is an isomorphism.
All geometric stalks of the counit are isomorphisms. Conservativity of geometric stalks gives the asserted isomorphism of abelian etale sheaves.
